Subject: Inspector Request – Photo Documentation for Legacy U-Haul Permit (Mesa) (01/27/26)

 

Team,

I wanted to document a conversation I had this morning with Gilbert Chavez, Temp Building Inspector II with the City of Mesa, regarding a legacy permit:

Record: PMT19-11810
Project: U-Haul
Address: 457 S Higley Rd, Mesa, AZ 85206


Gilbert advised that, as part of closing out inspections on this older permit, the city is requesting photo documentation showing:

*	The electrical disconnect switch serving the sign
*	The primary conductors properly secured and supported

From a code standpoint, these requests align with the adopted 2023 NEC, including:

*	NEC 600.6 – Disconnecting means required for electric signs
*	NEC 300.11 – Securing and supporting of raceways and conductors
*	NEC 110.12 – Mechanical execution of work (general workmanship)


Gilbert indicated that providing clear photo documentation of these items will allow the city to verify compliance without additional site visits, which is increasingly how Mesa (and other jurisdictions) are handling follow-up on legacy permits.


As a broader takeaway, this is another example of why photo surveys are becoming standard practice. Having organized, labeled photo documentation readily available goes a long way in:

*	facilitating required inspections,
*	reducing back-and-forth with inspectors,
*	and building long-term goodwill with jurisdictions and inspection staff.


Moving forward, continuing to treat photo surveys as a standard part of our process—especially for electrical and serviceability items—will help streamline closeouts like this.


I’ll coordinate the requested photos for this permit and keep everyone posted if anything further is needed.


Thanks,

Steve Skye

body:
<https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeYILzcwwgX6c13cnafWTmnPkJTcd9bRXyN-0GL5oPTKBEp_H4tD8hbJKB4P008ivekTeFlipRgEGdS5xoBnzO_Du7LmVD31Yy4bwwu8wx-bLS2PUtrKGaW2M7r22I5td8vFhlM?key=G9QUEyUqKnLMY_Oo3ZFD-w> 
 	 
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Friday, Jan. 23, 2026

CONTACT:
Cindy Casaus, Assistant Director & Chief of Communications

  

Unlicensed Peoria Man 

Sentenced for Fraud and Theft Charges

  

PHOENIX, Ariz., (Jan. 23, 2026) - On December 4, 2025, Steve Aaron Venegas, 53, of Peoria, Arizona pleaded guilty in Maricopa County Superior Court to two Fraud and three Theft charges, both Class 2 felonies. 

On January 7, 2026, Venegas was sentenced to 12 years in the Arizona Department of Corrections, plus 7 years of intensive probation.

The charges resulted from Arizona Registrar of Contractors (AZ ROC) investigations that found Steve Aaron Venegas dba Steve’s Landscaping of Peoria, Arizona was acting in the capacity of an unlicensed entity by performing hardscaping services without a contractor’s license. 

Venegas was the subject of 2 complaints in 2023. An additional 17 complaints were filed in 2024 after media coverage highlighting abandonment issues caused by Venegas aired. An additional 12 complaints were filed by homeowners in 2025, resulting in a total of 31 investigations.  

During these investigations it was discovered that Venegas would obtain a deposit for his work, would fail to finish or perform any work, and would insist that property owners make additional payments to conclude the work. 

The AZ ROC commonly receives complaints regarding unlicensed entities exploiting homeowners ranging from poor work to complete abandonment. If the entire cost of the project, including labor and materials is over $1,000, or requires a permit by the local municipality, Arizona Revised Statute 32-1121 requires the person or business performing the work to be licensed. The AZ ROC reminds home and property owners to always check the license before hiring a contractor by visiting roc.az.gov <https://click-1617733.icptrack.com/icp/relay.php?r=37004434&msgid=244763&act=6394&c=1617733&pid=620219&destination=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.roc.az.gov%2F&cf=11519&v=2b603a135b3daff6ee8bce1e5b597469f1ab62da21502405d27c88127dc28087>  or by giving our agency a call at 1-877-692-9762.

subject: Update - Scooter’s 2597 monument sign
body:
Hi Tony & Alex,

 

                Here is side by side by side.  

 

The 8’ tall sign is the max height of ground sign the lot can have per code.  

 

Then you must follow all the required setbacks needed in between the back of sidewalk & multi use trail and see if that 8’ tall sign will fit for placement.  It does not fit per code at all in that space & per city email was not recommended to place any sign there and to go behind the trail.

 

Need 5’ setback from back side of sidewalk and min. 3’ away from front of trail.  8’ of setbacks.   If we have 12’ in between these two points for sure.   Then sign max width can be 4’ max.  See pdf for that one.

 

FYI - This is if indeed there is 12’ wide area between back side of sidewalk and front side of trail And you clear all the in ground utilities in that exact spot (see below from GC) & you get city to accept new landscaping plan to move a few items from that exact spot for the new smaller monument location and find new spots on lot to replace those plants & Maybe have to re-submit new landscape plan to city for review and approval (TBD by Others) & that those other plants that stay all along the front that would be around the shorter sign don’t over grow and block it (See photo below).

 

If you only have 11’ of space, then after setbacks we can do about a 3’ max wide sign.  See pdf for that one.

                

FYI - FROM GC - Yes, there is water lines, electrical, and drip lines in that area.  Need to be careful when digging the footing -Todd.

 

Hope this helps.

Subject: RE: Crumbl–Peoria - Allowed Sign Area Confirmation (01/16/26) 
 

Hi Sarah,



Thanks for the question — this is a good one.


I reviewed both the City of Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) to confirm the allowable sign area for this location.


Although the tenant frontage is approximately 25 feet, the City of Phoenix code provides a minimum wall sign allowance of 50 square feet for commercial tenants. This comes directly from Phoenix Sign Ordinance Table D-1, which states:



“Wall Signs – Commercial: 1 square foot of sign area per 1 linear foot of building frontage (minimum 50 square feet).”


Because the ordinance establishes a 50 sq ft minimum, the normal frontage-based calculation (25 LF = 25 sq ft) does not apply here.


The Metro Towne Center CSP does not reduce this allowance — it regulates sign type and design standards, not overall area. The CSP permits aluminum pan channel letters for shop tenants and defers to the city ordinance for allowable square footage.  Based on both the Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the CSP:



• The maximum allowable area for the Crumbl primary wall sign is 50 square feet
• This allowance applies even with a 25’ tenant frontage
• Flush-mounted channel letters up to 50 sq ft total are permitted


You can therefore size the letters and logo however needed, provided the overall sign copy fits within a 50 sq ft envelope.


Please let us know if able to be of any additional assistance.


Warm regards,

Subject: RE: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 

 

Sarah,


Yes — your understanding is correct.


Under the Metro Towne Center CSP, the key requirement is that the sign copy be aluminum pan channel letters and not a cabinet-style sign box. 

The CSP does not prohibit raceways or backer panels — it regulates the sign type, not whether the letters are mounted directly to the wall, to a mesh raceway, or to a solid raceway.


Tropical Smoothie is a good example of this. Their sign uses individual channel letters mounted to a solid raceway, which is allowed under the CSP, just as the mesh-style raceways used by Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, and Dickey’s are allowed. Crumbl can follow either approach.


So, for Crumbl:

*	The letters must be individual aluminum pan channel letters
*	They may be mounted to a painted mesh or solid raceway
*	The raceway should be painted to match the wall or approved background color
*	A beige background will be acceptable, subject to City approval, just as it is for Tropical Smoothie


As long as the drawings clearly show channel letters on a painted raceway (not a cabinet), the design will be CSP-compliant and should satisfy the City’s correction without requiring a Minor Amendment.

Subject: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 

 

Hi Sarah,

We received the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) from the City of Phoenix today and completed our review in response to the EPR correction on the Crumbl – Peoria project.


Based on the CSP, we found the following with respect to the City’s comments:


The CSP prohibits cabinet-style sign boxes, but it allows tenant signage to be constructed as individually mounted aluminum pan channel letters. The CSP regulates the sign copy type, not the mounting method, and it does not prohibit raceways.


We have attached a CSP Compliance Exhibit documenting multiple existing tenants at Metro Towne Center — including Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, Dickey’s Barbecue Pit, Cold Stone, and MetroPCS — all of which use individual LED channel letters mounted to mesh or box raceways. These were approved under the same CSP and establish the accepted construction standard for this center. Accordingly, the Crumbl sign will be CSP-compliant when constructed as:

• Individually illuminated aluminum pan channel letters
• Mounted to a painted mesh or box raceway consistent with existing tenants
• No cabinet or translucent sign box
• Installed within the approved building sign band


This configuration satisfies both the CSP and the City’s correction and does not require a Minor Amendment.


Once Silicone Signs updates the drawings to this configuration, we can proceed with resubmitting the package to EPR.

Subject: RE: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 
 

Sarah,


Yes — your understanding is correct.


Under the Metro Towne Center CSP, the key requirement is that the sign copy be aluminum pan channel letters and not a cabinet-style sign box. 

The CSP does not prohibit raceways or backer panels — it regulates the sign type, not whether the letters are mounted directly to the wall, to a mesh raceway, or to a solid raceway.


Tropical Smoothie is a good example of this. Their sign uses individual channel letters mounted to a solid raceway, which is allowed under the CSP, just as the mesh-style raceways used by Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, and Dickey’s are allowed. Crumbl can follow either approach.


So, for Crumbl:

*	The letters must be individual aluminum pan channel letters
*	They may be mounted to a painted mesh or solid raceway
*	The raceway should be painted to match the wall or approved background color
*	A beige background will be acceptable, subject to City approval, just as it is for Tropical Smoothie


As long as the drawings clearly show channel letters on a painted raceway (not a cabinet), the design will be CSP-compliant and should satisfy the City’s correction without requiring a Minor Amendment.

Subject: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 

 

Hi Sarah,

We received the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) from the City of Phoenix today and completed our review in response to the EPR correction on the Crumbl – Peoria project.


Based on the CSP, we found the following with respect to the City’s comments:


The CSP prohibits cabinet-style sign boxes, but it allows tenant signage to be constructed as individually mounted aluminum pan channel letters. The CSP regulates the sign copy type, not the mounting method, and it does not prohibit raceways.


We have attached a CSP Compliance Exhibit documenting multiple existing tenants at Metro Towne Center — including Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, Dickey’s Barbecue Pit, Cold Stone, and MetroPCS — all of which use individual LED channel letters mounted to mesh or box raceways. These were approved under the same CSP and establish the accepted construction standard for this center. Accordingly, the Crumbl sign will be CSP-compliant when constructed as:

• Individually illuminated aluminum pan channel letters
• Mounted to a painted mesh or box raceway consistent with existing tenants
• No cabinet or translucent sign box
• Installed within the approved building sign band


This configuration satisfies both the CSP and the City’s correction and does not require a Minor Amendment.


Once Silicone Signs updates the drawings to this configuration, we can proceed with resubmitting the package to EPR.

Hi Steve:

 

*	https://youtu.be/nLxu5M4n9wM
*	https://youtu.be/nLxu5M4n9wM

 

This article addresses how to use the virtual fax feature, enabling users to send, receive, view, download, share, and delete faxes through desktop, mobile apps, email, or API. Key prerequisites include having fax storage enabled in system settings and virtual fax permissions granted by an admin.

 

**Main Issue:**

How to properly manage virtual faxes using different platforms while understanding permissions, file limitations, and geographic availability.

 

**Key Steps:**

 

1. **Before You Begin:**

   - Ensure fax storage is enabled.

   - Confirm you have virtual fax permissions (admin-enabled).

   - Note that faxes are stored up to 90 days; large files (over 10MB) delete after 21 days.

   - Virtual fax service covers 50+ countries, with some regional restrictions.

 

2. **Using Desktop/Web App:**

   - Sign in, select Phone > Fax from the sidebar.

   - If Fax option is missing, ask admin to enable your permissions.

   - Preview faxes (first page only), download, mark as read/unread, or delete (if permitted).

   - To send a fax: click +, choose sender fax number, enter recipients (up to 50), optionally add cover page, subject, and notes.

   - Attach supported file types (max 40MB, up to 500 pages).

   - Review and send; transmission failure notifications are sent via email.

 

3. **Using Mobile App:**

   - Sign in and select Fax from the bottom menu.

   - Share, download, view details, delete faxes similarly to desktop.

   - Send faxes by selecting +, entering recipients, attaching files, and sending as with desktop app.

 

4. **Sending Fax via Email:**

   - Compose new email with address formatted as faxNumber@‹domain›.fax.goto.com.

   - Attach supported file types (max 40MB, up to 500 pages).

   - Review and send; transmission failure notifications are sent via email.

 

3. **Using Mobile App:**

   - Sign in and select Fax from the bottom menu.

   - Share, download, view details, delete faxes similarly to desktop.

   - Send faxes by selecting +, entering recipients, attaching files, and sending as with desktop app.

   - Compose new email with address formatted as faxNumber@‹domain›.fax.goto.com.

   - Cover pages and sender fields can be customized.

subject: RE: Fax Setup on Copier/Scanner
body:
Hi Steve:

 

*	https://youtu.be/nLxu5M4n9wM
*	https://youtu.be/nLxu5M4n9wM

 

This article addresses how to use the virtual fax feature, enabling users to send, receive, view, download, share, and delete faxes through desktop, mobile apps, email, or API. Key prerequisites include having fax storage enabled in system settings and virtual fax permissions granted by an admin.

 

**Main Issue:**

How to properly manage virtual faxes using different platforms while understanding permissions, file limitations, and geographic availability.

 

**Key Steps:**

 

1. **Before You Begin:**

   - Ensure fax storage is enabled.

   - Confirm you have virtual fax permissions (admin-enabled).

   - Note that faxes are stored up to 90 days; large files (over 10MB) delete after 21 days.

   - Virtual fax service covers 50+ countries, with some regional restrictions.

 

2. **Using Desktop/Web App:**

   - Sign in, select Phone > Fax from the sidebar.

   - If Fax option is missing, ask admin to enable your permissions.

   - Preview faxes (first page only), download, mark as read/unread, or delete (if permitted).

   - To send a fax: click +, choose sender fax number, enter recipients (up to 50), optionally add cover page, subject, and notes.

   - Attach supported file types (max 40MB, up to 500 pages).

   - Review and send; transmission failure notifications are sent via email.

 

3. **Using Mobile App:**

   - Sign in and select Fax from the bottom menu.

   - Share, download, view details, delete faxes similarly to desktop.

   - Send faxes by selecting +, entering recipients, attaching files, and sending as with desktop app.

 

4. **Sending Fax via Email:**

   - Compose new email with address formatted as faxNumber@‹domain›.fax.goto.com.

   - Use the external 10-digit fax number without the leading 1 or dashes.

   - Include virtual fax machine’s access code in the Subject line.

   - Remove all text from email body except attachments.

   - Attach supported file types and send.

   - Confirmations depend on admin settings; failure notices are always emailed.

 

5. **API Use:**

   - Access fax listing, viewing, and deletion.

   - Useful for dashboard building, status monitoring, document syncing, and reporting.

 

6. **Additional Notes:**

   - Fax numbers must be formatted internationally.

   - Add @goto.com, @jive.com, and @jivecommunications.com to email allowlist to prevent notification emails from being marked as spam.

   - Cover pages and sender fields can be customized.

   - Fax cancellation is not possible once sent.

 

This guide ensures users understand how to set up, send, receive, and manage virtual faxes securely and efficiently across platforms with attention to administrative permissions and file limitations.

 

Doug Hill

602-663-5520

Subject: RE: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 

 

Sarah,


Yes — your understanding is correct.


Under the Metro Towne Center CSP, the key requirement is that the sign copy be aluminum pan channel letters and not a cabinet-style sign box. 

The CSP does not prohibit raceways or backer panels — it regulates the sign type, not whether the letters are mounted directly to the wall, to a mesh raceway, or to a solid raceway.


Tropical Smoothie is a good example of this. Their sign uses individual channel letters mounted to a solid raceway, which is allowed under the CSP, just as the mesh-style raceways used by Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, and Dickey’s are allowed. Crumbl can follow either approach.


So, for Crumbl:

*	The letters must be individual aluminum pan channel letters
*	They may be mounted to a painted mesh or solid raceway
*	The raceway should be painted to match the wall or approved background color
*	A beige background will be acceptable, subject to City approval, just as it is for Tropical Smoothie


As long as the drawings clearly show channel letters on a painted raceway (not a cabinet), the design will be CSP-compliant and should satisfy the City’s correction without requiring a Minor Amendment.


Warm Regards,

• Individually illuminated aluminum pan channel letters
• Mounted to a painted mesh or box raceway consistent with existing tenants
• No cabinet or translucent sign box
• Installed within the approved building sign band


This configuration satisfies both the CSP and the City’s correction and does not require a Minor Amendment.

Cc: Scott Frazer <scott@christysigns.com>
Subject: Crumbl – Metro Towne Center CSP Review & Design Direction (01/13/26) 
 

Hi Sarah,



We received the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) from the City of Phoenix today and completed our review in response to the EPR correction on the Crumbl – Peoria project.


Based on the CSP, we found the following with respect to the City’s comments:


The CSP prohibits cabinet-style sign boxes, but it allows tenant signage to be constructed as individually mounted aluminum pan channel letters. The CSP regulates the sign copy type, not the mounting method, and it does not prohibit raceways.


We have attached a CSP Compliance Exhibit documenting multiple existing tenants at Metro Towne Center — including Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, Dickey’s Barbecue Pit, Cold Stone, and MetroPCS — all of which use individual LED channel letters mounted to mesh or box raceways. These were approved under the same CSP and establish the accepted construction standard for this center. Accordingly, the Crumbl sign will be CSP-compliant when constructed as:



• Individually illuminated aluminum pan channel letters
• Mounted to a painted mesh or box raceway consistent with existing tenants
• No cabinet or translucent sign box
• Installed within the approved building sign band


This configuration satisfies both the CSP and the City’s correction and does not require a Minor Amendment.


Once Silicone Signs updates the drawings to this configuration, we can proceed with resubmitting the package to EPR.


Best regards,



Steve Skye

Hi Sarah,


Good morning and happy Friday.


We’ve received the City’s correction comments for the Back Nine sign permit resubmittal and wanted to clarify what they’re asking for.


The corrections are being issued because the submittal does not clearly document compliance with the master sign program requirements in an explicit way.


They’re looking for clearer confirmation of:

*	Final letter dimensions, spacing, and overall sign size (not shown as “estimated”)
*	Verification that the total sign area complies with master sign program limits
*	Explicit identification of materials, colors, and finishes as MSP-compliant
*	Clear installation and mounting details for halo illumination
*	Additional clarity on the hanging/arcade sign dimensions and mounting
*	Property owner authorization documentation


In short, the design concept is aligned with the master sign program, but the resubmittal needs to remove ambiguity and clearly state compliance rather than implying it.

We’ve received the City’s correction comments for the Back Nine sign permit resubmittal and wanted to clarify what they’re asking for.


The corrections are being issued because the submittal does not clearly document compliance with the master sign program requirements in an explicit way.


They’re looking for clearer confirmation of:

*	Final letter dimensions, spacing, and overall sign size (not shown as “estimated”)
*	Verification that the total sign area complies with master sign program limits
*	Explicit identification of materials, colors, and finishes as MSP-compliant
*	Clear installation and mounting details for halo illumination

*	Property owner authorization documentation

Hi Alex & Tony,

 

                The original site plans did have the blue sign box marked there with no scaled-out size or exact call out for width just a blue box on the site plans (which you can still see on our sign BB site plan See Below) between the back side of sidewalk and front side of trailhead.    Which is normal when we get site plans to show sign in general spot.

 

Once we were brought into to site and given those site plans to start and create a signage BB & most importantly do city code check – talk to GC about trailhead – check with city on trailhead, etc. to make sure sign could go there and ow large.

 

It was determined that in order to meet all city requirements (fyi who ever produced these site plans showing the sign box there might not have done this in depth city sign code check like we did in order to properly show it to scale for how large the finished size can be to meet current sign code and or were it would need to sit as well to meet all the code) the sign was going to be too small and not fit a 12’ tall typical.   See below for code.

 

1st we have to be behind property line.  No problem there.

 

2nd closer to the drive entry we get we must stay out of the triangle view clearance area marked red on my site BB site plan.  Again, no problem.

 

3rd we have to have a min. 5’ setback from the back side of sidewalk to the front edge of monument sign.   

 

4th we also have to maintain a 3’ either on front side of back side of trailhead clearance

 

Once we do the above items and if we do for sure have 12’ feet in between at the widest gap then that means the max widest part of the sign could have only been 4’ wide (Again if we do indeed have 12’).

 

4’ wide max sign would be about a 5’-0 tall with 18 s.f. area Vs. current sign in current spot that can then max out its height at 8’ tall per code with a copy area of 31 S.F.

 

FYI – Also to consider if we do go with shorter less S.F. sign to place in that small gap if we do have 12’ wide.

 

Landscape Plan approved by city – May need to be modified to get those current plants placed elsewhere 1st as we needed to use an city approved one during permit approval process and they might require a new one.

 

Utility Site One Call needs to be done to confirm any public and or private utilities in that slight curve area are clear to dig footing there.

Subject: Update - Scooter’s 2597 monument sign 

 

Hi Alex & Tony,

 

                The original site plans did have the blue sign box marked there with no scaled-out size or exact call out for width just a blue box on the site plans (which you can still see on our sign BB site plan See Below) between the back side of sidewalk and front side of trailhead.    Which is normal when we get site plans to show sign in general spot.

 

Once we were brought into to site and given those site plans to start and create a signage BB & most importantly do city code check – talk to GC about trailhead – check with city on trailhead, etc. to make sure sign could go there and ow large.

 

It was determined that in order to meet all city requirements (fyi who ever produced these site plans showing the sign box there might not have done this in depth city sign code check like we did in order to properly show it to scale for how large the finished size can be to meet current sign code and or were it would need to sit as well to meet all the code) the sign was going to be too small and not fit a 12’ tall typical.   See below for code.

 

1st we have to be behind property line.  No problem there.

 

2nd closer to the drive entry we get we must stay out of the triangle view clearance area marked red on my site BB site plan.  Again, no problem.

 

3rd we have to have a min. 5’ setback from the back side of sidewalk to the front edge of monument sign.   

 

4th we also have to maintain a 3’ either on front side of back side of trailhead clearance

 

Once we do the above items and if we do for sure have 12’ feet in between at the widest gap then that means the max widest part of the sign could have only been 4’ wide (Again if we do indeed have 12’).

 

4’ wide max sign would be about a 5’-0 tall with 18 s.f. area Vs. current sign in current spot that can then max out its height at 8’ tall per code with a copy area of 31 S.F.

 

FYI – Also to consider if we do go with shorter less S.F. sign to place in that small gap if we do have 12’ wide.

 

Landscape Plan approved by city – May need to be modified to get those current plants placed elsewhere 1st as we needed to use an city approved one during permit approval process and they might require a new one.

 

Utility Site One Call needs to be done to confirm any public and or private utilities in that slight curve area are clear to dig footing there.

 

 



Best,

subject: Update - Scooter’s 2597 monument sign
body:
Hi Alex & Tony,

 

                The original site plans did have the blue sign box marked there with no scaled-out size or exact call out for width just a blue box on the site plans (which you can still see on our sign BB site plan See Below) between the back side of sidewalk and front side of trailhead.    Which is normal when we get site plans to show sign in general spot.

 

Once we were brought into to site and given those site plans to start and create a signage BB & most importantly do city code check – talk to GC about trailhead – check with city on trailhead, etc. to make sure sign could go there and ow large.

 

It was determined that in order to meet all city requirements (fyi who ever produced these site plans showing the sign box there might not have done this in depth city sign code check like we did in order to properly show it to scale for how large the finished size can be to meet current sign code and or were it would need to sit as well to meet all the code) the sign was going to be too small and not fit a 12’ tall typical.   See below for code.

 

1st we have to be behind property line.  No problem there.

 

2nd closer to the drive entry we get we must stay out of the triangle view clearance area marked red on my site BB site plan.  Again, no problem.

 

3rd we have to have a min. 5’ setback from the back side of sidewalk to the front edge of monument sign.   

 

4th we also have to maintain a 3’ either on front side of back side of trailhead clearance

 

Once we do the above items and if we do for sure have 12’ feet in between at the widest gap then that means the max widest part of the sign could have only been 4’ wide (Again if we do indeed have 12’).

 

4’ wide max sign would be about a 5’-0 tall with 18 s.f. area Vs. current sign in current spot that can then max out its height at 8’ tall per code with a copy area of 31 S.F.

 

FYI – Also to consider if we do go with shorter less S.F. sign to place in that small gap if we do have 12’ wide.

 

Landscape Plan approved by city – May need to be modified to get those current plants placed elsewhere 1st as we needed to use an city approved one during permit approval process and they might require a new one.

 

Utility Site One Call needs to be done to confirm any public and or private utilities in that slight curve area are clear to dig footing there.

 

 



Best,

Hi Sarah,


We received EPR corrections from the City of Phoenix for Crumbl – Peoria (Job #27461), and I wanted to bring you up to speed.


The reviewer noted that this project is governed by the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP). Per their comments, cabinet signs are not permitted, and the CSP currently allows aluminum pan channel letters only. To proceed as-is, the sign would need to be revised to comply, or alternatively, a Minor Amendment could be pursued (which would require a narrative, additional review time, and a $270 fee).


That said, during our photo survey we did observe nearby tenant signs within the same center that appear to utilize mesh or open backers, which may indicate some flexibility under the CSP. Because of that, I’ve reached out to the City of Phoenix Sign Services Department (pdd.signservices@phoenix.gov <mailto:pdd.signservices@phoenix.gov> ) requesting clarification and asking how we can obtain a copy of the Metro Towne Center CSP for review.


Once we receive the CSP details or confirmation from the City, we’ll have a clearer path on whether a compliant mesh/backer option is feasible or if a formal amendment would be required.


I’ll keep you posted as soon as we hear back.


Best regards,

Plan Review Correction Task Assignment 
________________________________


Attention Steve:

This email serves as notification that the plan review for project number (251558-LPSG) is complete and corrections are required. The plans and comments can now be accessed by clicking on the "Login to ProjectDox" link below. You should have already received an email notification from "SB1598 DSD/DSD/PHX@PHXENT" containing additional information regarding this plan review. If you need further assistance please call the Payments and Submittals section at 602-534-5934.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-836 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over. With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review. If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal. Please visit our website for more information: phoenix.gov/pdd/licensetimes.html. 

Plan review correction cycles and plan approvals are valid for 180 days. Application for extension must be made and the fee paid PRIOR to the expiration date or a new plan review submittal and fee will be required. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: Completing the assigned ProjectDox WorkFlow Portal task sends the project back to the City of Phoenix. If the applicant does not complete their assigned task, City staff will not receive notice the project requires action.

3️⃣ Corrected set + checklist required for upload
Once the above items are corrected, the full package needs to be reassembled with:

*         Updated plan set

subject: Scottsdale's New Planning and Permitting Portal
sender_name: City of Scottsdale Planning and Development
body:
View In Browser <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/clickp?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a42_0x314c06x05354:::VIBPB:::&a3=1176&a2=STEVE%40CHRISTYSIGNS.COM&a0=5354&a4=STEVE%40CHRISTYSIGNS.COM&a1=%26AMP%3B%3B:::VIBPE:::> 

 <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a42_0x32812x05354> 	 

Scottsdale’s Planning and Development Services Department has launched a new planning and permitting portal. Scottsdale SPUR (Smart Planning, Use and Regulations) replaces the 30-year-old eServices system and provides customers with a user-friendly interface to submit development requests, plans, payments, and other documents for city processing.
 

Within the portal, customers will:

*	Submit project applications, plans and construction documents
*	Pay fees
*	Monitor project milestones
*	Receive permits
*	Schedule inspections
*	View records
	 

Behind the scenes, the new platform combines the permitting functions from across various city departments and disciplines into one streamlined system. City staff will:

*	Review submitted applications, plans, and documents
*	Note redlines
*	Approve plans
*	Process payments
*	Issue permits
*	Upload inspection notes
*	Issue Certificates of Occupancy
*	Manage records
	 

All new projects will now be submitted through Scottsdale SPUR. Applications and projects that are already in the Planning and Development queue will continue through the legacy eServices system.
 

Getting started with SPUR

Visit our Scottsdale SPUR webpage <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a42_0x314b17x05354>  to create an account, view the user guide, and get support from SPUR experts.
 

Continuing an existing project

Projects that were initiated before Jan. 6, 2026 will continue through the development process using the previous eServices system. Please visit the “eServices Portal” button located under the Online Tools section of the Planning & Development Services webpage <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a42_0x3af84x05354>  to find the eServices links for managing your project.

You may also visit us at ScottsdaleAZ.gov <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a42_0x343eex05354> . This email was sent to &EMAIL;.

Hi Sarah,



We received the City of Scottsdale’s notification that Back Nine (Plan Check 8852-25) has completed Review Cycle 1 and is now in CORRECTIONS status. I’ve attached the correction sheets along with the Master Signage Package referenced in the City’s notes. Below is a concise breakdown of what must be addressed before the next submittal:

 

1️⃣ Provide landlord / property-management approval letter
The application is flagged as administratively incomplete because ownership approval is not yet on file. A signed approval must accompany the corrected package.

2️⃣ Update artwork and elevations per MSP standards
Key alignment items called out by the reviewer include:

*         Letter height limits — Must comply with the MSP dimensional maximums; current submittal exceeds the allowable size (see MSP pg. 2).

*         Tenant elevation formatting — Required elevation format and façade call-outs must follow MSP exhibit style (MSP pg. 12–13).

*         Hanging sign installation details — Installation height above grade and bracket mounting detail must be shown (correction sheet pg. 3).

*         Window graphic requirements
• Provide area calculations (total square footage)
• Confirm percentage of transparency / open-view requirement
• Identify material type and method of application (film vs. lettering)

3️⃣ Corrected set + checklist required for upload
Once the above items are corrected, the full package needs to be reassembled with:

*         Updated plan set

*         Landlord approval letter

*         Completed City resubmittal checklist

*         Any supplemental specifications referenced (materials, illumination specs, etc.)


I’ll prepare the actual portal resubmittal once the corrected plan set and landlord approval are in hand.


Let me know if you’d like a quick call to review the corrections together before the revisions begin.

subject: 2026 Group Plan Medicare Notice (CMS Letter)
body:
To Any Employee/Dependent that is Medicare Eligible:

The Medicare Modernization Act (MMA) requires entities (whose policies include prescription drug coverage) to notify Medicare eligible policyholders whether their prescription drug coverage available through their group plan is creditable coverage, which means that the coverage is expected to pay on average as much as the standard Medicare prescription drug coverage.

This annual Medicare disclosure, also known as a CMS letter, must be provided to Medicare eligible active working individuals and their dependents, Medicare eligible COBRA individuals and their dependents, Medicare eligible disabled individuals covered under the group prescription drug plan, and any retirees and their dependents. The MMA imposes a late enrollment penalty on individuals who do not maintain creditable coverage for a period of 63 days or longer following their initial enrollment period for the Medicare prescription drug benefit. Accordingly, this information is essential to an individual’s decision whether to enroll in a Medicare Part D prescription drug plan.

For your convenience, GLJ has posted the CMS letter(s) for your available plan option(s) to your Employee Navigator account to help you determine whether or not the group plan you enrolled in is creditable or not.

If you have any questions about the CMS letter(s) posted to your Employee Navigator, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our office.

Regards,

The GLJ Team

subject: Weekly Pool Service Report
body:
Weekly Pool Service Report


Customer: Dane Christensen
Service Address: 14207 North 69th Drive, Peoria, AZ 85381 

Service Date: December 31st, 2025    Tech: Caleb
Service Time: 2:06pm



Service Summary:

Hello Dane, Caleb visited your pool on December 31st, 2025, and carried out a comprehensive maintenance check to ensure your pool remains in great condition. During the visit, Caleb performed routine tasks such as skimming, brushing, emptying the skimmer and pump baskets, and conducting chemical testing. The water chemistry readings showed that free and total chlorine levels are at 1 ppm, which is within the ideal range for free chlorine but on the lower end for total chlorine. The pH level is perfect at 7.2. Cyanuric acid is currently at 15 ppm, lower than the recommended range, while total alkalinity is 120 ppm, which is ideal. Calcium hardness is at 100 ppm, which is below the preferred range for cooler months. Caleb added one chlorine tab to help maintain appropriate chlorine levels. During a visual inspection, Caleb noted that the backwash outer cap is cracked, rendering the pool pump temporarily inoperable. Please avoid turning on the pump until the replacement part is installed on January 2nd, 2026. Rest assured, your pool is being carefully maintained, and we look forward to our continued service.

subject: Enrollment Completed
body:
I hereby apply for all non-contributory coverage(s) under my employer's plan and any contributory coverage(s) that I have elected this online application. I understand and agree that due to payment of my premiums (deductions) on a pre-tax basis and unless a qualifying event occurs, that my benefit elections above cannot be changed until my employer's next open enrollment. 
Life and/or disability income: I understand that I must satisfy the eligibility and actively at work requirements at my employer's usual place of business on the date of coverage for myself and any eligible dependents, before coverage.s become effective. If I am not actively at work, I understand that coverage for myself and life coverage for my eligible dependents may not become effective until I return to work. I will be considered a late applicant if I decline any contributory coverage offered under this application and later apply. As a late applicant applying for coverage, I understand that proof of good health may be required for myself and eligible dependents. 
Flexible Benefits Account Coverage: If I have elected to redirect money for eligible dependent care expenses, I have considered the IRS tax credit available to me. I understand that if I am married and filing a separate tax return, a lower maximum applies. 
Health coverage: I understand that I must submit a Certificate or evidence of prior creditable coverage to receive credit towards the satisfaction of any pre-existing condition limitation specified in my employer's plan; and to be eligible for credit, the gap between the two coverage(s) must be 62 days or less. I and/or my eligible dependent(s) will be considered a "Special Applicant" if:

*	I did not previously elect to cover myself and/or my eligible dependent(s) under my employer's policy/plan because of other health coverage and I later apply because the coverage terminated involuntarily; or
*	I did not previously elect to cover myself and/or my eligible dependent(s) and I later apply for coverage because of a change in my family status resulting from marriage, birth or adoption of a child.

I understand that to qualify as a "Special Applicant" I must apply for health coverage for myself and/or my eligible dependent(s) within 31 days after:

*	Coverage under the prior health plan ends; or I marry; or I acquire a new child through birth, adoption or placement of a child for adoption.

I will be considered a late applicant if:

*	I fail to qualify as a "Special Applicant" because I did not apply within the 31 days as specified above; or
*	I did not previously elect to cover myself and/or my eligible dependents and I later apply.

As a late applicant applying for health coverage, I realize that I may only be allowed entrance to the plan during the open enrollment period. As a late applicant, I realize that my entry to the plan may be subject to special enrollment requirements and that I must contact my Plan Administrator for details. 
For all coverage(s): I hereby authorize any insurance company, health care provider, or other entity or person having knowledge of anyone listed on this application to give this new carrier or their designated agent(s) any and all records pertaining to such person's medical history for purposes of review, investigation or evaluation. For application purposes, this authorization is valid for 30 months from the date I sign it. For purposes of claims, reimbursement and receipt of services rendered, this authorization is valid during the term of such person's coverage for evaluation of the nature and medical necessity of the services received. I am, or my authorized representative is, entitled to a copy of this signed authorization. By submitting this application online, I hereby consent to receiving all important, plan-related documents and notices through this electronic medium, and agree to share access to these documents with my dependent spouse, if applicable and enrolled. These important documents include the plans. Summary Plan Descriptions, Summary of Material Modifications, Summary Annual Reports, and Summary of Benefits and Coverage. The important notices include your Notice of Special Enrollment Rights, Notice of Availability of COBRA Coverage, Medicaid/CHIPRA Notice, Women.s Health and Cancer Rights Act Notice, General Notice of Pre-Existing Conditions, and a HIPAA/HITECH Privacy Notice, and can be found on this site. Your consent to receiving this information electronically may be withdrawn at any time, without charge, by notifying your company administrator. You may also request paper copies of any document or notice, free of charge. You will need to have Adobe Acrobat Reader software to view these important documents and notices.
I also acknowledge that I have read and understand the important information regarding Cobra and HIPAA disclosure information. This Disclosure Information forms a part of the Application for Membership as fully as if it were contained over the applicant's signature. 




Thank you,

Subject: Signage Limitations for Wendler Parcels – City of Tempe (GID Zoning) 

 

Hi Rocky,

I wanted to update you on the signage restrictions for the Wendler parcels (4415 & 4625 S Wendler Dr, Tempe), based on our review of the City of Tempe Zoning and Development Code and confirmation from Mike Scarpitta of the Tempe Sign Department.


Both parcels are zoned GID (General Industrial District) and are not part of any PAD or Development Plan. As such, they are limited to standard monument-style freestanding signs under Tempe ZDC §§ 4-901–4-904.

Here are the key points:

*	Maximum sign height: 8 ft
*	Maximum sign area: 24 sq ft per face
*	Type: Monument or architectural base design (masonry/stucco finish to match building)
*	Freeway/high-profile signs: Only permitted through a recorded Development Plan or PAD overlay—these Wendler parcels do not qualify under current zoning.
*	Address numerals: Minimum 6″ high required on the base.


Mike confirmed that the larger “freeway monument” signs along the I-10 corridor were approved decades ago as part of their original Development Plans and are effectively grandfathered. 

The Wendler properties were not included in those agreements, so the City will enforce the 8' / 24 sq ft limitation.


Attached is the full Sign Ordinance Report – Tempe Wendler Parcels (GID) summarizing these findings, citations, and code references for our records.


Best regards,

subject: Merry Christmas! Our Holiday Schedule Update
body:
Hello Dane,

The holidays are just around the corner, and we want to take this time to wish you and your loved ones a very Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year! We’re grateful for the opportunity to care for your pool and for your continued trust throughout the year.

To allow our team to spend quality time with their friends and family, NextGen Pool Care will be closed next week, from Monday, December 22nd through Sunday, December 28th. This means there will be no regular pool maintenance or appointments during that week. We will resume normal service the following week.

We will also be closed on New Year’s Day (Thursday, January 1st). If your regular pool service is scheduled for New Year’s Day, we’ll take care of your pool on Friday, January 2nd instead. All other service days will remain the same.

Thank you so much for being a valued part of the NextGen Pool Care family. We appreciate your understanding.

Warm regards,

The NextGen Pool Care Team

subject: Scottsdale Planning and Development - Phishing Scam Alert
sender_name: City of Scottsdale Planning and Development
body:
View In Browser <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/clickp?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x314b12x05303:::VIBPB:::&a3=3847&a2=STEVE%40CHRISTYSIGNS.COM&a0=5303&a4=STEVE%40CHRISTYSIGNS.COM&a1=%26AMP%3B%3B:::VIBPE:::> 

 <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x32812x05303> 	 

Dear Scottsdale Planning and Development Services Customer,
 

We have become aware of an email phishing scam where the sender is posing as our department. While the email messages vary in content, the request is the same: respond to the email for instructions on wiring funds.
 

The messages may appear authentic as they reference recent planning and development cases and board and commission decisions. However, there are key indicators of it being a scam.

1.	The email address comes from "planning-scottsdaleaz.gov @usa.com"
	City communications will always have an @ScottsdaleAZ.gov domain name as the suffix. While scottsdaleaz.gov is within the email address, it has a usa.com suffix which indicates it is not an official city of Scottsdale email.
2.	The email requires you to reply for a payment link and instructions. Fee payments will always be collected through our secure website portal or in person at the One Stop Shop. Visit our Planning and Development Services webpage for the accurate city of Scottsdale portal links.

Please be aware that on Jan. 6, 2026, we will be launching a new planning and permitting portal, Scottsdale SPUR. Projects that have been initiated before this date will continue to use the Community Development System "eServices" portal to manage your project. Projects initiated after this date will start in Scottsdale SPUR. Learn more about this new system by visiting the City of Scottsdale’s website, ScottsdaleAZ.gov, and searching “Scottsdale SPUR <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x314b17x05303> ” or visiting the Planning and Development Services <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x3af84x05303>  homepage.
 

If you receive a message you believe to be a phishing scam, please forward it to Planning and Development Services’ systems analyst Angel Gonzalez at AGonzalez@ScottsdaleAZ.gov <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x314b15x05303> .
 

Customers are encouraged to call our department at 480-312-3111, or the planner assigned to your case, for information related to your project.
 

Please do not reply to this message as it was sent from a mailbox that is not monitored. 

You may also visit us at ScottsdaleAZ.gov <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/click?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x35690x05303> . This email was sent to &EMAIL;.

Unsubscribe or manage your email subscriptions <https://newsletters.scottsdaleaz.gov/trk/clickp?ref=zvbdm4r20_1-32csrvn-0-2a24_0x31ab7x05303&t=&EMAIL;> .

Hello, 

 

Thank you for your interest obtaining a business in the Town of Guadalupe. I’m happy to guide you through the business license process.

 

Along with your completed application, please include:

 

*	A copy of a valid photo ID

 

*	Your Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) License number (with Guadalupe listed as a region/jurisdiction)

 

*	A copy of your Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license (most current, the one provided is from 2013.

body:
Hello Brian, 

Thank you for your reply. 

I will check into this and get back to you by Friday . 

Wendy Christensen 
Christy Signs 

Get Outlook for iOS <https://aka.ms/o0ukef> 
________________________________

From: Brian Larson <Brian.Larson@tucsonaz.gov>
Sent: Monday, December 8, 2025 12:59:39 PM
To: wendy@christysigns.com <wendy@christysigns.com>
Cc: steve@christysigns.com <steve@christysigns.com>
Subject: CHRISTY SIGNS / T0094181 
 
Good afternoon Wendy,

Based on your email I reviewed the account as well as the filed tax returns for Christy Signs. 

A "Candiso Christensen" signed a 09/2014 tax return on 10/16/2014 showing activity and stated that there was $32.50 due in sales tax to the city of Tucson however it was never paid.  This same individual signed and submitted multiple sales tax returns in 2015 and 2016 showing activity.  That is where we are coming up with the figures that are showing tax is due.

Were these returns filed in error?  If so we would need amended tax returns showing the error.  Also please advise if this license needs to be cancelled and if so what date should be listed as the last day the company operated business in Tucson.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns.




Thank you,

 

Brian Larson

Taxpayer Assistance - Revenue Investigations

Direct Phone: 520-837-4455
Office Hours: Monday - Friday, 8:30am - 5:00pm
Address: 201 N Stone Avenue, 5th Floor ~ Tucson AZ 85701

subject: RE: Habit Burger - Prasada/Surprise
body:
Steve,  

 

So you have it also, attached is the last email exchange I had with Ken McNeeley, who seems to have been tasked with addressing the City’s violation related to the building repaint and the murals.  I had coordinated with him before for some info on the murals, which resulted in a little blurb narrative they put on the plans, and I need some additional info or statements.  The use of murals is a gray area for Surprise with the Prasada DRC allowing them, but they need to be unique and artistic as opposed to obvious commercial messaging or branding.   If they end up being something that isn’t unique and really just for attention grabbing, we just consider them as signs and part of the business’ allowed sign area, so I had asked them to get me more info.   I am not too concerned about the color pattern on the east elevation unless we find out that they will be replicating this on any store they can, but the random sun on the west elevation, may be counted as a sign… but there is plenty of sign area allowance available.  

 

 

 



Andy Jochums, AICP

Senior Planning Consultant

Gilbert Blilie PLLC

701 N. 44th Street | Phoenix, AZ 85008

Direct: 480.429.3063 | Main: 480.429.3000

Email: ajochums@gilbertblilie.com <mailto:ajochums@gilbertblilie.com>

Cc: Scott Frazer <scott@christysigns.com>; Kelly Lepkowski <klepkowski@everbrite.com>
Subject: RE: Habit Burger - Prasada/Surprise

 

Hi Andy,

Thank you for the clarification and for sending over the original approved sign plans and mural information.


We will be informing Everbrite, Habit Burger’s sign vendor, that any changes from the original approved package—including the clearance bar, directionals, removal of “Drive-Thru,” and the murals—must be submitted to the Prasada DRC for review and approval before anything goes back to the City of Surprise.


I’ll reach out to Everbrite to review these requirements with them and determine how they would like us to proceed on the updated sign package and DRC submittal. Once we have a plan and the necessary revisions, I’ll follow up with you regarding the next steps.


Thank you again for your guidance and assistance.

subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] U-Haul Sahuarita - Comprehensive Sign Plan (12/08/25)
body:
Steve,

I have provided information on the Comprehensive Sign Plan below. Please fill out the attached application as well. Planning and Zoning Commission meetings are the first Monday's of the month so February 2nd would be your goal.
In order to make that meeting we would need to have the advertisement to the newspaper approximately 3 weeks before the meeting date. Your application with all required materials needs to be submitted really by the end of this month so we can review it. If it is not in by then you are looking at the March meeting date.

We do not have a separate form for the Comprehensive Sign Plan. The sign code does specifically state what is required in your application, which is listed below.

2. Required Elements. The comprehensive sign plan shall provide the following information:
a. A design theme with illustrative examples of each sign type.
b. The location, size, height, construction materials, color, type of illumination, and orientation of all existing and proposed signs.
c. Maximum numbers of tenant panels per sign face.
d. For all freestanding signs, setbacks from right-of-way and property lines.
e. For all attached signs, clearance below and context of placement on facades.
f. Total proposed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project.
g. Maximum allowed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project, and explanations of how the maximums were calculated.
h. If the applicant proposes a deviation from the standards set forth in this chapter, the following additional information shall be provided:
(1) A detailed explanation of the deviations being proposed.
(2) A written justification for the deviations.

The code also explains what needs to be met in order to get the extra 20 percent.

With planning and zoning commission approval at a public hearing noticed per STC 18.91.060 <https://www.codepublishing.com/AZ/Sahuarita/#!/Sahuarita18/Sahuarita1891.html#18.91.060> (A), a comprehensive sign plan may allow signage in which the total sign area budget for each sign type and height of freestanding signs exceeds the maximum otherwise allowed by five percent for each criterion met, up to a maximum of 20 percent. In no event may the comprehensive sign plan propose signage of a type that is otherwise prohibited by this chapter, and in no event may the height, number, or size of freeway-style signs exceed the maximum otherwise allowed. Increases in sign area budgets for a sign type or freestanding sign height shall be based on the following criteria:
a. An additional five percent for use of one or a combination of the following options in all illuminated signage:
(1) Halo illumination, prohibiting the use of white or off-white/ivory light sources; or
(2) Prohibition of the use of predominantly white or off-white/ivory internally illuminated lettering, logos or trademarks.
b. An additional five percent when each sign is related to all other signs maintained on the site by the incorporation of similar or identical elements, such as materials, sign copy, letter styles, color, illumination, method of attachment, and overall presentation.
c. An additional five percent for the use of native or natural, or native- or natural-look, sign construction materials or colors that are reflective of the surrounding desert and mountain environment, the purpose of which is improved and innovative sign design and an improved image of the use or development; a minimum of 75 percent of the sign structure shall be constructed of such native or natural, or native- or natural-look, materials.
d. An additional five percent for a sign plan that relates in form, proportion, scale, color, materials, surface treatment, overall sign size, and the size and style of the lettering to the function and architectural character of the building or premises on which they will be displayed, and which provides for signs that are placed in a logical location in relation to the overall composition of the building’s facade and do not cover any key architectural features or details of the facade.

Additional information can be found in the Town code using the following link:

https://www.codepublishing.com/AZ/Sahuarita/#!/Sahuarita18/Sahuarita1879.html#18.79

Thanks,
Dylan

Dylan Parry, AICP
Senior Planner
Community Development

Good afternoon Wendy,

Based on your email I reviewed the account as well as the filed tax returns for Christy Signs. 

A "Candiso Christensen" signed a 09/2014 tax return on 10/16/2014 showing activity and stated that there was $32.50 due in sales tax to the city of Tucson however it was never paid.  This same individual signed and submitted multiple sales tax returns in 2015 and 2016 showing activity.  That is where we are coming up with the figures that are showing tax is due.

Were these returns filed in error?  If so we would need amended tax returns showing the error.  Also please advise if this license needs to be cancelled and if so what date should be listed as the last day the company operated business in Tucson.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns.




Thank you,

 

Brian Larson

Cc: Kevin O'Neil <koneil@cazfire.gov <mailto:koneil@cazfire.gov> >; Dan Trout <dtrout@chinoaz.net <mailto:dtrout@chinoaz.net> >; Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com> >
Subject: 718 S State Route 89 _ 306-29-035B (CL) - Proposed storage tank plo

 

	Caution: This e-mail is from an external sender. Please use caution when clicking links or opening attachments. When in doubt, please click the Phish Alert button. 

 

Hi Dave,

 

Thank you for your call this morning.

 

As discussed, you mentioned that Inspector Kevin O’Neil provided a letter approving the new storage tank location, confirming the minimum 20-foot building separation and that a 4-foot setback from the property line is acceptable. I’ve copied Mr. O’Neil so he can provide that letter and advise if any additional information or a pre-application meeting is needed. I’ve also copied our Building and Safety Official, Mr. Dan Trout, for input on the 4-foot separation.

Regarding site lighting: As noted during the sign approval process and in recent conversations, several fixtures remain visible from the public right-of-way, which is a concern given the highway frontage. You confirmed this morning that all lights will be turned off today and that your contractor will ensure any replacements are dark-sky compliant (downlit and under 5,000 lumens). This is a required condition of approval per Resolution 2025-1294 (attached). If significant lighting changes are planned, I recommend submitting a photometric plan with your updated site plan so we can review both items together for UDO compliance.

 

I know the church is hoping to open for service to the public soon, and it would be a shame for any lingering issues to prevent opening in the next few month . As a reminder, the system cannot issue permits or final inspections sign offs  when a code violation is open. Turning the lights off in the interim should help prevent a case from being opened—thank you for addressing that promptly. I’ve copied Mr. Skye with the sign company so they are aware as well.

 

To move forward, please reply with:

• An updated site plan showing the new tank location
• Fire and building clearance documents (including Inspector O’Neil’s letter)
• A lighting/photometric plan with cut sheets for any replacement, altered, or added outdoor fixtures

 

I appreciate your cooperation and look forward to your response.

 

Kind regards,
Jess

 

 

Jessica Barragan

Senior Planner

Alex,

 

                On the exact placement of your retention area & trailhead (& per any city requirements on these items) that would be Arch & Civil Eng questions who worked on project to be sure you can move it.  

 

I would not have any city code knowledge of these items they worked out with city during the front side development to know if they can be moved.

 

But I would bring in the Civil Eng. & Arch as well before you move trailhead into retention area to make room for sign between back of side plus 2’ then    

 

They are now on email chain as well as permit officer for Christy signs Steve who may need to submit on his end as well.

 

Below is the original site plan showing sign in between trailhead and back of sidewalk.  As you can see the box that was on site plan that is supposed to represent the sign is sandwiched between sidewalk & trailhead.

 

When we scaled this out when doing Brand Book to place sign on lot and meet all code, we could no way get sign in between there like shown.

 

I do see your logic.  If you can get the trailhead pushed into retention area, then we can put sign back in that spot and get the needed 2’ setback.

 

If you do this and push trailhead south to gain room.  What I don’t know as of now, is that, is there a city setback from sign base to front side of trailhead like the back side of trailhead of 5’?

 

If so, then between 2’ setback from sidewalk, 5’-4” wide already made base & maybe 5’ front side trailhead setback.  

 

Would need about 12’-4” at min. in between sidewalk and trailhead to place sign there.

 

 



 

Best,

Subject: 718 S State Route 89 _ 306-29-035B (CL) - Proposed storage tank plo

 

	Caution: This e-mail is from an external sender. Please use caution when clicking links or opening attachments. When in doubt, please click the Phish Alert button. 

 

Hi Dave,

 

Thank you for your call this morning.

 

As discussed, you mentioned that Inspector Kevin O’Neil provided a letter approving the new storage tank location, confirming the minimum 20-foot building separation and that a 4-foot setback from the property line is acceptable. I’ve copied Mr. O’Neil so he can provide that letter and advise if any additional information or a pre-application meeting is needed. I’ve also copied our Building and Safety Official, Mr. Dan Trout, for input on the 4-foot separation.

Regarding site lighting: As noted during the sign approval process and in recent conversations, several fixtures remain visible from the public right-of-way, which is a concern given the highway frontage. You confirmed this morning that all lights will be turned off today and that your contractor will ensure any replacements are dark-sky compliant (downlit and under 5,000 lumens). This is a required condition of approval per Resolution 2025-1294 (attached). If significant lighting changes are planned, I recommend submitting a photometric plan with your updated site plan so we can review both items together for UDO compliance.

 

I know the church is hoping to open for service to the public soon, and it would be a shame for any lingering issues to prevent opening in the next few month . As a reminder, the system cannot issue permits or final inspections sign offs  when a code violation is open. Turning the lights off in the interim should help prevent a case from being opened—thank you for addressing that promptly. I’ve copied Mr. Skye with the sign company so they are aware as well.

 

To move forward, please reply with:

• An updated site plan showing the new tank location
• Fire and building clearance documents (including Inspector O’Neil’s letter)
• A lighting/photometric plan with cut sheets for any replacement, altered, or added outdoor fixtures

 

I appreciate your cooperation and look forward to your response.

 

Kind regards,
Jess

subject: Could MCPs be your MVP?
body:
Go behind the buzz on this new AI standard.
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtPsvC8J63GzA9BHUn1RMHxyofgGo0EAq4gzBCaCvdADDJCesE-IwHKmjoU4G3Z6wybY=>  
DIGITAL BUILDER 
It’s easy to overlook how much AI connectivity has leveled up in the construction industry alone, but the changes happening now are unignorable. For years, getting AI to do something useful meant giving it a ton of context. That’s now shifting dramatically. With Model Context Protocol (MCP), tools can now communicate more intelligently, making workflows smoother and decisions faster. And now MCP servers are taking things even further, opening the door to a whole new level of interoperability.

In this edition, we break down what MCP servers are, why they matter, and how they’re setting the stage for a future where connected systems just work.
	
 	 
IN TODAY'S EDITION: 

*	The fundamentals of what construction pros should understand about MCPs <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtP7i6RiWY_3nsCNbvnxhuWAjmVx_RPhChEuXMuUUAaJrvejBppSbz1fogel1y2Fv-vA=> .
*	A deep dive into what's next for MCP servers in construction <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtBjeapkheiEo5dB76cVHzM0xK29xnd-Y4sERjHIz6Awi7tPRSCA-7ADyXkgJYkJe5n4=> .
*	Beyond MCPs, construction pros share some surprising truths about AI and digital twins <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtLA426fpsGjEra9RRDIVprpvwYOAfVx4E1Zz98bNQcrOOjVKsrb8CacAkud4wCyuJcI=> .

PODCAST: What every construction professional should know about Model Context Protocols	 
Artificial intelligence is transforming the way we work — but until recently, its capabilities were limited by context. Enter Model Context Protocol (MCP), a new standard that’s changing the game by enabling AI agents to connect directly with external tools and data sources.

In this episode of Digital Builder, we sit down with Ben Cochran, Vice President of Engineering at Autodesk, to demystify MCPs and explore what they mean for construction workflows. Recorded live at Autodesk University 2025 in Nashville, this conversation dives into why MCPs are generating so much buzz and how they’re unlocking new levels of efficiency across the industry.
	
Tune in <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtP7i6RiWY_3nsCNbvnxhuWAjmVx_RPhChEuXMuUUAaJrvejBppSbz1fogel1y2Fv-vA=>  	
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtBjeapkheiEo5dB76cVHzM0xK29xnd-Y4sERjHIz6Awi7tPRSCA-7ADyXkgJYkJe5n4=>  
The future of construction workflows with MCP servers	 
Complexity in construction only continues to rise driven by environmental constraints, regulatory compliance, supply chain costs, and talent gaps. To stay competitive, designers and builders must navigate this complexity strategically, and increasingly, they are turning to agentic AI. Agents are systems that can not only reason and synthesize information – like we often see with assistants like ChatGPT or Gemini – but these systems can also make decisions and execute on the outcomes that we define for them. And now, agents can connect to different data and tools using Model Context Protocol (MCP), which is a big leap forward in what’s possible with AI in construction. This blog explores what MCP servers are, why they matter, and how they can reshape construction workflows.	 
Explore what's next <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtBjeapkheiEo5dB76cVHzM0xK29xnd-Y4sERjHIz6Awi7tPRSCA-7ADyXkgJYkJe5n4=>  	
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtLA426fpsGjEra9RRDIVprpvwYOAfVx4E1Zz98bNQcrOOjVKsrb8CacAkud4wCyuJcI=>  
4 surprising truths about AI and digital twins, according to industry leaders	 
The conversation around artificial intelligence and digital twins in the AECO industry is reaching a fever pitch. But amid the buzzwords and bold predictions, a more nuanced reality is taking shape. To cut through the noise, a recent industry panel brought together four experts at Autodesk University to ground the discussion in practical application, revealing a landscape that is more accessible, sustainable, and human-centric than the hype suggests. This blog distills the key insights from that conversation, backed by comprehensive industry data.	 
Unlock insights <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGehEYFtLA426fpsGjEra9RRDIVprpvwYOAfVx4E1Zz98bNQcrOOjVKsrb8CacAkud4wCyuJcI=>

Hi Dave,

 

Thank you for your call this morning.

 

As discussed, you mentioned that Inspector Kevin O’Neil provided a letter approving the new storage tank location, confirming the minimum 20-foot building separation and that a 4-foot setback from the property line is acceptable. I’ve copied Mr. O’Neil so he can provide that letter and advise if any additional information or a pre-application meeting is needed. I’ve also copied our Building and Safety Official, Mr. Dan Trout, for input on the 4-foot separation.

Regarding site lighting: As noted during the sign approval process and in recent conversations, several fixtures remain visible from the public right-of-way, which is a concern given the highway frontage. You confirmed this morning that all lights will be turned off today and that your contractor will ensure any replacements are dark-sky compliant (downlit and under 5,000 lumens). This is a required condition of approval per Resolution 2025-1294 (attached). If significant lighting changes are planned, I recommend submitting a photometric plan with your updated site plan so we can review both items together for UDO compliance.

 

I know the church is hoping to open for service to the public soon, and it would be a shame for any lingering issues to prevent opening in the next few month . As a reminder, the system cannot issue permits or final inspections sign offs  when a code violation is open. Turning the lights off in the interim should help prevent a case from being opened—thank you for addressing that promptly. I’ve copied Mr. Skye with the sign company so they are aware as well.

 

To move forward, please reply with:

• An updated site plan showing the new tank location
• Fire and building clearance documents (including Inspector O’Neil’s letter)
• A lighting/photometric plan with cut sheets for any replacement, altered, or added outdoor fixtures

 

I appreciate your cooperation and look forward to your response.

Jess

We need it to be as visible as possible for cars driving from East and West and we need to be aware of the trees around the area, and the parking lot in the liquor store that may block views. If we need to resubmit to get a better place or the best place we should consider this because a monument is not required for opening and it's very expensive and we kind of only get the decision to put it in the best place possible only once.

But again, priority is the install of all of the other things! We have our electric and IT team coming out and need monument signs, wall signs etc.

Alex

subject: city of Buckeye Permit has been issued - BLDC-25-0336
body:
Your permit is now in Issued status, and the approved plans and documents are available online through the Citizen Self-Service (CSS) Portal. Inspections can be scheduled online through the portal. Please follow the instructions below to access, print your permit, and download approved plans.

 

How to Print a Permit 

1.	Log in to the CSS Portal: City of Buckeye <https://egselfservice.buckeyeaz.gov/energov_prod/selfservice#/home>  

	*	Note: Registration is required to access records. If you do not have an account, you must create one before proceeding.

2.	Locate Your Permit: 

	*	Click on the “Dashboard” tab.
	*	Find your permits under “My Permits”, or use the search bar to locate them.
	*	Click the permit record to open the permit details.

3.	Print the Permit: 

	*	Locate and Click the Printer Icon at the top right section of the screen.

 



 

How to Download Approved Plans

1.	Access the Permit Record (Follow Steps 1-2 above)
2.	Go to the “Attachments” tab within the permit record.
3.	Click on each approved file to download.

 

Important Notes:

*	You must be logged in to access permit documents and schedule inspections.
*	If you cannot view your records, please email permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov <mailto:permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov>  or call our office at 623-349-6200 for assistance.

subject: Thanksgiving Holiday Schedule Update
body:
Hello Dane,

As Thanksgiving approaches, we want to take a moment to express our gratitude for your trust and support throughout the year. We are truly thankful for wonderful customers like you!

To allow our team to spend quality time with their families and friends, NextGen Pool Care will be taking the week of Thanksgiving off. This means our service technicians will not be performing regular pool maintenance or appointments from November 23rd through November 29th. Our regular service schedule will resume the following week.

We appreciate your understanding and flexibility as we make this adjustment to our schedule. If you have any specific concerns about your pool during this time, please don’t hesitate to reach out to us in advance.

Thank you again for being a valued part of the NextGen Pool Care family. Wishing you and your loved ones a happy and safe Thanksgiving!

< p>

Warm regards,

The NextGen Pool Care Team

subject: RE: Sign Permit Application Inquiry - LPSG 251389 (Jas Diesel) (11/20/25)
body:
Hello,

the only thing the previous approval can provide is the solace that this new submittal will eventually get approved if all corrections are met.

 

Proposed sign A falls in a public utility easement. To keep sign in proposed location, please provide sign off from every utility company operating in this easement. This will also require the owner to move and reinstall this sign at their expense should any work need to be performed in this area.

 

*	You’ll need to complete a blue stake survey and contact every utility company operating in this easement for sign off to allow this ground sign here.

 

Proposed sign A exceeds the maximum height allowed by sign code 705 table D1, commercial land use. Please lower overall sign height to 16 feet. To keep as proposed, submit for design review. the fee is $150; the review time is 2 weeks and requires a written narrative.

Additional reason for design review – site plan requirement. All site plans created after 1992 require ground signs to submit for design review. All reasons for design review will be included in the written narrative and will only a one-time fee.

 

*	You’ll need design review approval to allow an additional height of 20 ft. this will require a written narrative and the fee of $150 before this review can start.

 

Hope this clears some things up.

 

Thank you,
